tasks.title: The h function
tasks.statement: Write h(type, props, ...children) → { type, props, key, children }. props is null or an object: the result contains a copy of the props without key; key is taken from props.key (or undefined). Children are normalized: nested arrays are flattened recursively; null, undefined, true and false are dropped; strings and numbers become { type: '#text', text: String(value) } (0 is kept); objects (ready-made vnodes) are added as they are. The input props is not mutated.
tasks.hint: A helper add(c) that recurses into arrays; pull key out of the copy of the props.

tasks.title: classNames
tasks.statement: Write classNames(...args): builds a class string. Arguments: strings and numbers are taken as they are (non-empty; 0 is skipped as falsy), arrays are processed recursively, objects contribute keys with truthy values; null, undefined, false and empty strings are skipped. The result is the classes separated by a single space in order of appearance; duplicates are not removed.
tasks.hint: An inner add(a) that dispatches on the type.

tasks.title: Style object → string
tasks.statement: Write styleToString(style): the object's properties, in key order, become "name:value" joined by ";" (no spaces and no trailing ";"). Names are converted camelCase → kebab-case (backgroundColor → background-color). Numbers get "px", except zero and unitless properties (opacity, zIndex, lineHeight, flex, flexGrow, flexShrink, order, fontWeight). Values null, undefined and false are skipped. An empty object gives an empty string.
tasks.hint: Replace with /[A-Z]/ for the names; a set of unitless properties.

tasks.title: Render to an HTML string
tasks.statement: The h function is already provided. Write renderToString(vnode): text is escaped (& < > → & < >); an element is "<type attributes>children</type>"; void elements (area, br, col, hr, img, input, link, meta, source) are "<type attributes>" with no closing tag and no children. Attributes go in property order: values are escaped (& < > "), true gives an attribute with no value (the name only), false/null/undefined and on* handler props are skipped; class is a string or an array of strings (joined with a space); style is an object: "name:value" joined by ";" (camelCase → kebab; for simplicity, do not add units to numbers). A space before the attributes is added only if there are any.
tasks.hint: Recursion: text → escape, element → collect attrs and children.

tasks.title: Parse HTML into vnodes
tasks.statement: The h function is already provided. Write parseHtml(html) → an array of top-level vnodes (created via h). Supported: tags with attributes (values in double or single quotes, unquoted ones run up to a space or ">", a boolean attribute is true), void elements (area, br, col, hr, img, input, link, meta, source), "<tag/>" as self-closing, text, and the entities & < > " in text and in values. Text nodes consisting only of whitespace are dropped; for the others, leading and trailing spaces are kept as they are. A closing tag must match the open one, otherwise Error('Mismatched closing tag </x>'). An unclosed tag at the end gives Error('Unclosed tag <x>').
tasks.hint: Tokenize with a regular expression: <!?/?name ...>|text; keep a stack of open elements.

tasks.title: A {{ }} template with filters
tasks.statement: Write interpolate(template, data). The expression "{{ path | filter | filter:'arg' }}" is replaced with a value: path is keys separated by dots (array indices as numbers: items.0.name); a missing value gives an empty string. Filters apply left to right: upper, lower, trim, default:'text' (if the value is undefined, null or '', substitute the text), raw (disables escaping). Any other value is converted with String(). After the filters the result is escaped (& < > " to entities) unless raw was used. Spaces inside the braces and around "|" are ignored. An unknown filter gives Error('Unknown filter: name').
tasks.hint: replace(/\{\{(.*?)\}\}/g, …); split the path on dots; filters via split('|').

tasks.title: From a vnode to DOM nodes
tasks.statement: The DOM model (MiniNode, doc, dump), h, classNames and styleToString are already provided. Write createDom(vnode, doc) → MiniNode. Text: doc.createText(text). Element: doc.createElement(type); then go through the props in key order: null, undefined and false are skipped; on* (onClick…) → el.addListener(event name in lowercase without "on", function); class → setAttr('class', classNames(value)); a style object → setAttr('style', styleToString(...)); true → setAttr(name, ''); anything else → setAttr(name, value). Then the children are created recursively and added with append.
tasks.hint: Handle the props by the rules and add the children recursively.

tasks.title: Props diff
tasks.statement: Write diffProps(oldProps, newProps) → an array of operations. First the removal operations { op: 'remove', name } for keys that are absent from the new props (in alphabetical order), then { op: 'set', name, value } for new keys and keys whose value changed (Object.is), also in alphabetical order. Function values are compared by reference. Equal values produce no operations.
tasks.hint: Two passes over the sorted keys.

tasks.title: Tree diffing
tasks.statement: The function diffProps is already provided (remove/set operations). Write diff(oldV, newV) → a patch or null (no changes). Rules: no old node (null/undefined) → { type: 'CREATE', node: new } (if there is no new one either → null); no new node → { type: 'REMOVE' }; type or key differ → { type: 'REPLACE', node: new }; both are text: if the text differs → { type: 'TEXT', text }, otherwise null; otherwise (same type and key): props = diffProps(old.props, new.props), and children is an array of patches by index (the length is the larger of the two lengths; null for unchanged ones). If props is empty and all children are null, the result is null; otherwise { type: 'UPDATE', props, children }.
tasks.hint: Diff the children recursively by index; do the CREATE/REMOVE/REPLACE checks first.

tasks.title: Applying patches to the DOM
tasks.statement: The DOM model (MiniNode, doc, dump), h, createDom and diff are already in the starter. Write applyPatch(parent, index, patch, doc): it applies a patch (in the diff format) to the node parent.children[index]. CREATE: insert createDom(node) at position index (insertAt); REMOVE: remove parent.children[index]; REPLACE: replace it with createDom(node) (replaceChild); TEXT: replace the node's text field; UPDATE: apply props to the node (set: for on*, unsubscribe the old function (it cannot be learned from the props, so keep it in node.__props) and subscribe the new one; class/style as in createDom; true → ''; false/null/undefined: remove the attribute; remove: remove the attribute and the handler) and then apply the children's patches: first all non-REMOVE ones in ascending index order, then the REMOVE ones in descending index order. null patches are skipped. For the old props use node.__props, which createDom in the starter fills in.
tasks.hint: For UPDATE: get node = parent.children[index]; handle props; then the children in the required order, recursively (the parent is node).

tasks.title: Matching lists by keys
tasks.statement: Write reconcileKeys(oldKeys, newKeys) → { removed, created, moves }. removed: keys absent from the new list (in old-list order); created: new keys that did not exist before (in new-list order); moves: the elements to move by the "last placed index" algorithm (as in React): walk the new list; for a key that was in the old list, take its index in the old list, oldIndex; if oldIndex < lastPlaced, the element must be moved: add { key, to: index in the new list }; otherwise lastPlaced = oldIndex. New keys do not affect lastPlaced. Keys are unique.
tasks.hint: A Map from key to old index; a single pass over newKeys.

tasks.title: Longest increasing subsequence
tasks.statement: Write lis(arr): returns an array of indices (ascending) of the longest strictly increasing subsequence of an array of numbers. If there are several, pick the one whose index sequence is lexicographically smallest (that is, take the earliest possible first index first, then the earliest possible second index, and so on). An empty array gives [].
tasks.hint: f[i] is the length of the LIS starting at i (computed from the end); then greedily choose the earliest indices with the needed f.

tasks.title: Minimum moves
tasks.statement: The function lis(arr) (indices of the longest strictly increasing subsequence; among equal ones, the lexicographically smallest indices) is already provided. Write minMoves(oldKeys, newKeys) → an array of keys that must be moved, in new-list order. Only keys present in both lists are considered: take them in new-list order, turn them into old indices, find the LIS of those indices; the corresponding keys stay in place, and all the other (common) keys must be moved. Keys present in only one of the lists are ignored.
tasks.hint: common = newKeys.filter(present in the old list); idx = common.map(k => oldKeys.indexOf(k)); stay = lis(idx).

tasks.title: Syncing handlers
tasks.statement: The DOM model (MiniNode with addListener/removeListener) is in the starter. Write syncEvents(node, oldProps, newProps): for every handler prop (a name of the form on + capital letter…: onClick, onInput) bring the node's listeners in line. The event name is the part after "on" in lowercase (onClick → click). If the function has changed (by reference): unsubscribe the old one (if there was one) and subscribe the new one (if there is a function). Prop removed: unsubscribe. Props that are not handlers are ignored. Handlers that have not changed must not be touched (the number of listeners must not grow).
tasks.hint: Walk the union of the keys; for on* compare the old and new functions.

tasks.title: memo for components
tasks.statement: Write memo(component, equals = shallowEqual): wraps a component function component(props). The wrapper W(props) returns component(props), but if props are equal (per equals) to the previously passed ones (on the first call there is nothing to compare with), it returns the previous result (the same reference) instead of calling. W has a counter W.renders, the number of times component was actually called, and W.reset(), which forgets the cache. Define shallowEqual(a, b) yourself: the same set of keys and values equal by Object.is (nested values by reference).
tasks.hint: Store lastProps and lastResult; clear them on reset.

tasks.title: Mini hooks: useState and useMemo
tasks.statement: Write createRuntime(): { render(Component, props), update(), useState, useMemo }. render(Component, props) remembers the component and the props, calls Component(props) with the "current runtime" and returns the result. Inside a component, hooks work in call order (slots persist between render/update): useState(initial) → [value, setState] (initial may be a function, called once; setState(v | fn(prev)) stores the value, and if it changed (Object.is), marks the runtime "dirty"); useMemo(fn, deps) recomputes fn only if deps changed (element by element with Object.is; the first call always computes) and returns the value. update(): if the runtime is dirty, calls the last component again with the same props, clears the flag and returns the new result; otherwise returns null. Hooks outside render give Error('Hooks can only be called inside a component').
tasks.hint: An array of slots and an index reset before each component call; useState/useMemo take the slot by index.

tasks.title: Duplicate keys
tasks.statement: The h function is already provided. Write findDuplicateKeys(vnode) → an array of { path, key }: for every node with children, find the child nodes whose key !== undefined and whose key repeats among its children. One entry per repeated key (three equal ones still give one). path is a string of indices from the root joined by dots ("root", "root.0", "root.0.2": the index of the child in its parent) and points to the parent. Traversal is depth-first, left to right; for one parent, entries go in order of the first appearance of the duplicate.
tasks.hint: Recursion with path; a Map from key to its count among the children.

tasks.title: Minimal text edit
tasks.statement: Write diffText(a, b) → { start, deleteCount, insert }: the single edit that turns a into b: replace a.slice(start, start + deleteCount) with the string insert. Find the common prefix, then the common suffix (not overlapping the prefix), and return what lies between them. If the strings are equal: { start: a.length, deleteCount: 0, insert: '' }. The prefix is always taken as long as possible.
tasks.hint: First i is the prefix length; then j is the suffix length that does not run into the prefix.

tasks.title: Applying reorders to a DOM list
tasks.statement: The DOM model (MiniNode, doc, dump) and reconcileKeys(oldKeys, newKeys) (returns { removed, created, moves }) are already provided. Write patchList(list, newKeys, doc): list is a MiniNode list whose children are "li" elements with a data-key attribute and a text child (the key). Bring the children to the order of newKeys while keeping the existing nodes (by data-key): remove the nodes in removed; create nodes for created (createElement('li'), data-key = the key, one text child with the key); then arrange the children so that the order matches newKeys, calling insertAt only for the nodes that are not at the right position (nodes already in the right place must not be touched). Return { created: the number of created nodes, moved: the number of insertAt calls (including insertions of new nodes) }.
tasks.hint: Build a Map from key to node; then walk newKeys and for position i check list.children[i] === node.

tasks.title: Hydration check
tasks.statement: Write hydrateCheck(node, vnode): node is a MiniNode (server markup: fields tag, text, attrs, children), vnode is the client description ({ type, props, children }; text ones are { type: '#text', text }). Return an array of mismatches (strings) in depth-first order; the path is indices from the root joined by dots, the root is "0". Checks for a node, in order: type/tag ("PATH: tag mismatch (div vs span)", node.tag vs vnode.type; on a mismatch the children are not checked); for text, "PATH: text mismatch ("a" vs "b")" (JSON quotes); for elements, attributes: for every non-handler (not on*) prop of vnode whose value is not null/undefined/false, the expected string (true → '', a class array joined with a space) must equal node.attrs[name], otherwise "PATH: attribute id mismatch ("a" vs "b")" (a missing one is JSON null); then the child count "PATH: child count mismatch (2 vs 3)" (server first, then client), and the children are checked pairwise up to the minimum. Attributes go in props key order.
tasks.hint: A recursive function with path; first the tag, then attrs, then the count, then the children.

tasks.title: Batching update scheduler
tasks.statement: Write createBatcher(applyFn): returns a function enqueue(update) → Promise. update is any value (for example a function). enqueue accumulates updates; in the nearest microtask (queueMicrotask) applyFn is called once with an array of all accumulated updates in the order they were enqueued, after which all promises of that batch resolve with the value applyFn returned. Updates enqueued after it fires go into the next batch (a new applyFn call). An exception in applyFn rejects the promises of the batch (but the next batch works as usual).
tasks.hint: A queue and a scheduled flag; in the microtask take out the queue and call applyFn inside try/catch.

tasks.title: Lifecycle events
tasks.statement: The h function is already provided. Write lifecycleEvents(oldTree, newTree) → an array of strings. The trees are vnodes; only component nodes matter (type is a function; the name is type.name). Matching: at the same position (child index) and with the same type, "update NAME"; otherwise the old component gives "unmount NAME" and the new one "mount NAME". Event order: first all unmounts (a post-order traversal of the old tree, left to right: children before their parent), then mounts and updates in pre-order traversal of the new tree. Children are matched by index; a component's children are the children of its vnode (you do not need to call the function). No old tree (null): only mount; no new tree: only unmount. Non-component elements produce no events, but their children are still matched.
tasks.hint: Two phases: collectUnmounts(old, new) with a post-order traversal and collectMountsUpdates(old, new) with a pre-order one.

tasks.title: Fragments
tasks.statement: Write Fragment (a unique Symbol('Fragment')), h(type, props, ...children) and flatten(vnode). h works as usual: { type, props, key, children } with normalized children (arrays are flattened, null/undefined/true/false are dropped, strings and numbers → { type: '#text', text }). flatten(vnode) returns a new tree in which fragments among the children are replaced by their children (recursively, in the same order), and a root fragment is returned as an array of nodes; ordinary elements remain elements with cleaned children. Text nodes are returned as they are. flatten does not mutate the original tree.
tasks.hint: flattenChildren(children) expands nested fragments; a root fragment is flattenChildren(vnode.children).

tasks.title: The each and when helpers
tasks.statement: The h function is already provided. Write each(list, keyFn, renderFn), when(cond, thunk, otherwise = null) and match(value, cases, fallback = null). each returns an array of vnodes: for every element (item, index), the result of renderFn(item, index) with its key field set to keyFn(item, index) (the result of renderFn is a vnode; its key is overridden); a repeated key gives Error('Duplicate key: KEY'). when: if cond is truthy, thunk(); otherwise otherwise (a value or null; if otherwise is a function, call it). match: cases is an object "value → thunk"; if the key String(value) is in cases, call that thunk, otherwise fallback (called if it is a function, otherwise returned as it is).
tasks.hint: A Set to check keys; a helper call(x) = typeof x === 'function' ? x() : x.

tasks.title: HTML sanitizer
tasks.statement: Write sanitizeHtml(html, { tags, attrs }): tags is an array of allowed tags (lowercase), attrs is an object "tag → allowed attributes" (the key '*' applies to all tags). The input is simple markup: tags with attributes in double quotes, and text. Rules: a tag not in the list is removed (opening and closing), while its inner text and allowed nested tags stay; the exception is script and style, which are removed together with their content. An attribute not among the allowed ones is removed; attributes starting with "on" are always removed; href and src values that start (after trimming spaces, case-insensitively) with "javascript:", "data:" or "vbscript:" are removed together with the attribute. Other attributes are kept in the original order and form (name="value"). Text is not changed. Closing tags of allowed elements are kept as they are.
tasks.hint: Tokenize with the regular expression /<\/?[a-zA-Z][^>]*>|[^<]+/g; for script/style skip everything up to the closing tag.

tasks.title: Patch summary
tasks.statement: The patch format is the same as in diff: null | { type: 'CREATE', node } | { type: 'REMOVE' } | { type: 'REPLACE', node } | { type: 'TEXT', text } | { type: 'UPDATE', props: [{ op: 'set'|'remove', name, value? }], children: [patches] }. Write countOps(patch) → an object of counters { CREATE, REMOVE, REPLACE, TEXT, UPDATE, SET, UNSET }: all keys are always present (in this order); totals over the whole tree; SET and UNSET count the props operations (set and remove). null gives all zeros. Then write isCheap(patch, limit): true if the total number of operations (CREATE + REMOVE + REPLACE + TEXT + SET + UNSET; UPDATE is not counted) is no more than limit.
tasks.hint: Recurse over children; keep the counters in a single object.

tasks.title: Patches by path
tasks.statement: Patches are as in diff (null | CREATE | REMOVE | REPLACE | TEXT | UPDATE { props, children }). Write flattenPatches(patch): an array of records { path, type, ... } in depth-first order (a parent before its children). path is an array of child indices from the root (the root is []). For an UPDATE with non-empty props: a record { path, type: 'PROPS', ops: props }; then, recursively, the records of the children (path + [i]). For CREATE, REMOVE, REPLACE and TEXT: one record { path, type } plus the field node (for CREATE/REPLACE) or text (for TEXT). null produces no records. An UPDATE with no props and no meaningful children yields no records.
tasks.hint: A recursive function with an accumulator and the current path.

tasks.title: When to re-render
tasks.statement: Write shouldUpdate(prev, next, opts = {}) → boolean. Props comparison: the sets of keys must match; values are compared with Object.is, except: keys in opts.ignore are skipped; keys in opts.deep are compared deeply (arrays element by element, objects by keys, primitives with Object.is; there are no cycles); functions are compared by reference unless opts.ignoreFunctions === true (then any functions are considered equal). Returns true if a re-render is needed (the props differ).
tasks.hint: An inner deepEq; iterate over the union of keys, taking ignore/deep into account.

tasks.title: Serializing a vnode
tasks.statement: Write serializeVnode(vnode) → a JSON string, and deserializeVnode(str). Serialization: the keys of the vnode object and of props go in the order { type, props, key, children } and alphabetically for props; function values are replaced with the object { "$fn": name } (the function's name, or 'anonymous'); Symbol values with { "$sym": description }; undefined in props and in key is omitted (a vnode without a key has no key field); children are handled recursively. The string is JSON.stringify without spaces. deserializeVnode turns a string into an object (JSON.parse); functions and symbols stay as markers. No indentation.
tasks.hint: A recursive transform that checks typeof; JSON.stringify at the end.

tasks.title: Normalizing props into attributes
tasks.statement: Write normalizeProps(props) → { attrs, events, style }. Rules, in key order: className → the class attribute (a string, array or object, built as in classNames: falsy values are skipped; an empty result means no attribute); htmlFor → for; tabIndex → tabindex; readOnly → readonly; httpEquiv → http-equiv; the rest as they are (data-*, aria-* and so on). Booleans: true → an attribute with the value ''; false, null, undefined → no attribute is created. Numbers and strings become strings. The keys key and ref are skipped. Handler props of the form on + capital letter… go to events: { event name in lowercase without "on": function }. style: if it is an object, it is returned in the style field as it is, not in attrs; if it is a string, it goes to attrs.style. The style field is null if no object is given.
tasks.hint: A rename table; build the class string yourself.
